dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Sandra. Good morning, how can I help you?
Good morning, and thank you for taking my call. My name is Moira Flynn. I would like to open a small shop, and I am not certain what I need. Thank you.
Oh, how exciting! Okay, so a shop. What kind of shop are you thinking, Ms. Flynn?
Yes, thank you. Well, it would be a little shop selling secondhand linens and some china. Is that a business license, or is it a permit? I am afraid I do not know the difference. Thank you.

That's a fair question, a lot of people mix those up. For a retail shop you'd generally be looking at a business license through our office, and there may be a separate sign-off depending on the location, like zoning or inspections. Do you have a storefront picked out?
Not yet, no. I thought I should do the license first, and then find the place. Is that the correct order? Thank you.
Well, honestly, most folks get the space lined up first, because the license usually goes with a specific address. But I can walk you through the forms now so you're ready.
Oh. I see. I had it backwards, then. Thank you. And what forms would those be? I had understood there was one form, but my neighbor said two.

Your neighbor may be right. There's the application itself, and sometimes a second form for the type of business. I'd have you pick them up here so you get the right set. They're also at the counter at City Hall.
Thank you. And the fee, please? Is that paid when I hand in the form, or after they approve it? I am sorry, I am not sure how it works.
The fee depends on the kind of license, so I don't want to give you a number that's wrong. When you come in, the counter staff will tell you the exact amount, and you normally pay when you submit.
I see. So, the fee is at the counter. Thank you. And what should I bring with me, in person? Thank you.

Bring a photo ID, the address of the shop if you have it, and a lease or something showing you can use the space. If you have a name for the business, bring that too. A checkbook or card for the fee is smart.

A lease. Yes. Thank you. Now, I should say that I do not drive much, only my old minivan, and the sliding door sticks terribly. So I may need to take a bus. Is it a long walk from the stop? Thank you.
Oh, those sliding doors, they love to stick in the cold! The bus can get you pretty close to City Hall, and it's only a short walk from there. Take your time, we're open weekdays.
That is very kind. Thank you. So, to repeat it: the license comes after I have the space, and I bring identification and the lease. And the second form, is that the one for the zoning? Thank you.
Close. The zoning piece isn't always a form you fill out, it can be a check on the address. The counter will tell you if you need it. Don't worry, you'll be walked through it.
Oh. Then I am still a little unsure, but I will go in and ask. Thank you very much, Sandra. I appreciate your patience. Thank you.
Anytime, Ms. Flynn. Good luck with the shop, and have a lovely day.
You as well. Thank you. Goodbye.
